images.title: Fold, crease, unfold: a rhombus
images.purpose: Shows an unfolded sheet with its two fold lines crossing at the centre and the copied crease making a rhombus whose diagonals lie along the folds.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large sheet of paper in the centre with two fold lines and one rhombus crease pattern.
images.exact_structure: One rectangular sheet of paper, wider than tall, white with a thin dark outline. Two dashed grey (#6B7280) fold lines: one horizontal and one vertical, each through the centre of the sheet, crossing at right angles with a small square right angle mark at the centre. A rhombus drawn in thick teal (#0072B2) lines, centred on the crossing, with its four corners on the fold lines: the left and right corners on the horizontal fold, farther out, and the top and bottom corners on the vertical fold, closer in. Each of its four sides carries one identical short reddish purple (#CC79A7) tick mark. The label fold sits beside the horizontal fold line near the right edge, the label fold beside the vertical fold line near the top edge, and the label rhombus under the sheet. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A crease copied into four quarters makes a rhombus whose diagonals lie along the folds.
images.description: Shows an unfolded sheet with its two fold lines crossing at the centre and the copied crease making a rhombus whose diagonals lie along the folds.
images.context: If the crease cuts equal lengths on both folds, the diagonals are equal and the rhombus is a square.

image_decisions.why: The unfolded sheet shows at once why the four copied creases make four equal sides.
